notes: Most detailed account found of the church's EXTERIOR as it stood in 1904 (read in OCR). Cornerstone 21 Sept 1872; first services Jan 1873 (Sunday-school room) and 30 Nov 1873 (sanctuary); BELL TOWER COMPLETED 1884. 'The tower was originally topped by a graceful spire with a tall, slender finial, but these were lost due to wind damage in 1929' (the 1974 NRHP form instead says the tower's hipped roof was removed after a 1959 storm — conflict to resolve with dated photographs; either way the 1904 tower had a tall roof/spire). Church ~60 ft high; exterior 110 × 168 ft; nave about 72 × 116 ft; seats ~1,200. Fire of 9 March 1900 destroyed the roof and much of the nave interior; Shaw's rebuild LOWERED and flattened the nave roof (original 'more sharply pitched and its peak considerably higher'), and the east-wall rose window (La Farge round mosaic, destroyed 1900) was replaced. Exterior description: four-storey square tower with corner buttresses, open belfry with paired pointed arches and angel figures, corner gargoyles; central Gothic portal with head of Christ; five lancets and a large window under the gable with symbols of the Evangelists; north buttress pinnacle 'once topped by a tall finial'; north and south walls with three rows of windows (copper-framed opalescent clerestory, six large pointed windows, small windows below); north side brick; west transverse section with wheel window and copper oriel; mottled bituminous limestone laid in banded stringcourses.
